description.p: LDM is a download manager for Linux, modelled on 1DM for Android. Downloads keep running in a background service, so closing the window never stops them.

ul.li: Splits files into parts and downloads them over several connections
Pauses, resumes and retries; expired links can be replaced without losing progress
Downloads videos and streams, including YouTube, HLS and DASH (via yt-dlp)
Downloads torrents and magnet links, with file selection and seeding limits
Runs scheduled downloads in a time window and can wait for an unmetered connection
Has a browser extension for Firefox, Chrome and Brave

screenshot.caption: Downloads by category and queue, with the connections and details of the one in progress
The same downloads in dark style

ul.li: LDM for Windows 10 and 11, as a preview: an installer for your user (no administrator rights) with yt-dlp, FFmpeg and Node.js included, a tray icon, notifications, and start at login
On Windows, the browser extension works in Firefox, Chrome, Edge and Brave, magnet links and .torrent files open in LDM, and the ldm command works in any terminal
New commands: ldm quit stops the download service and closes the window; ldm version shows which yt-dlp, libtorrent, FFmpeg and JavaScript runtime LDM uses
A torrent counts as finished only once all its data is written to disk
A new window, built with Qt: menus and search, a toolbar, a sidebar with categories, queues and a speed graph, and a resizable details panel with each download's connections
Every dialog redone: Add, Settings, Schedule, Batch download, Checksum, Torrent details and more
Light and dark, following the system or chosen in View → Appearance
Ubuntu 24.04 and Linux Mint 22 now use the Flatpak (they lack the Qt libraries LDM needs)
Packages for Debian 13, Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04 (also Linux Mint 22) and Arch Linux, alongside Fedora
A Flatpak for every other distribution
The package is now called ldm-downloader; the command is still ldm, and on Fedora it replaces the old ldm package automatically
Runs on older GNOME libraries (libadwaita 1.5), so Ubuntu 24.04 and Linux Mint 22 are supported
Keeps yt-dlp up to date for each user, so YouTube downloads keep working where the distribution's yt-dlp is old
The browser extension works with more browser setups, and explains what to do with Snap browsers

description.p: Select several downloads to pause, resume, remove or delete them at once. Video streams with signed links now download: LDM sends the same request headers as the browser. The copied-link banner can be dismissed, and the tray icon is monochrome.
First release: multi-part downloads, video and torrent support, scheduler, browser extension.
